reason: AURA_PULSE: the aura periodically detonates for a burst.  The card's value is the burst SIZE in seconds-of-aura-DPS, so the cadence has to live here as a constant. Six seconds is long enough that the pulse reads as an event rather than as a slightly larger aura.

AURA_TRAIL: the aura leaves a damaging trail behind the player.  Dropped on a cadence rather than every frame, and only when the player has actually MOVED — a stationary cursor would otherwise stack every drop in one place and turn a trail card into a second aura.

Auto-travel, checked on a timer rather than on an event (2026-08-20).  It used to fire from ONE place: the moment a boss died. That was correct when a boss kill was what opened the next biome. Biomes have unlocked on Catnip earned this run since the floors change, and nothing emits "a threshold was crossed" — so for every biome without a boss in front of it, which is five of the eight, the checkbox did nothing at all. Reported as "autotravel doesn't work", and it did not.  Polled at AUTO_TRAVEL_POLL_SEC because the condition is a comparison between two continuously-moving numbers. A signal for it would have to fire on every Catnip tick, which is the pattern that just cost this game 90% of its frame rate.
Distance at which it counts as having arrived.
How far from the edges the boss will place itself.
How long the boss death sequence runs before anything else is allowed to happen. Matches Boss._play_death_sequence()'s shake + collapse.

The biomes that host a boss, in clear order. This list is the progression ladder — every other progression number is derived from it rather than from a tier number, which is what stops the old name-math ("tier N's boss grants stage N+1") from quietly reappearing once the counts stopped matching.  Ledger keys stay biome ids, not "boss_1".."boss_3": the ledger is saved, and re-keying it would silently un-clear every existing save.

a literal in Boss._tick_movement(): the idle drift target wanders up to this far across from the anchor, so the boss never looks parked

Mirrors CATCHES_BASE / CATCHES_GROWTH in tools/pawsim.py. Kept as constants rather than a .tres because the simulator parses the .tres files and would then be reading its own inputs back — these two numbers are calibrated in the simulator and copied here, so the copy is the thing that must not drift. check_cards.gd asserts the curve matches the simulator's closed form. Raised from 8.0 / 1.75 on 2026-08-18: "XP gain should be slower in the beginning". At base 8 the first card arrived after EIGHT mice, which is before the player has met the shop, the aura or a signature — the run had no opening, it had a card. The first level now costs 24.  BASE alone would have slowed every level by the same factor. GROWTH comes down a little as well so the extra cost lands hardest early and eases off: the first four levels cost ~2.7x what they did, the thirteenth ~1.6x.  NOT re-calibrated against the 10-15 picks-per-run band, deliberately — the designer asked for the mechanical changes first and one economy pass over all of them afterwards. Expect the pick count to have moved.

Carry: the aura radius bonus currently earned by holding still.  Capped at CARRY_FULL_SECONDS because an uncapped version rewards leaving the game alone, which is the one thing an idle game must not pay for directly - the cat is already idle, and a radius that grew forever would make not playing strictly better than playing.

CATNIP_BOMB_EVERY: every Nth kill detonates where the last mouse died.  Damage is expressed in SECONDS OF AURA DPS, like Pounce, rather than as a flat number. This is the failure mode that has bitten this project three times — a term that does not track the main curve does not stay small, it disappears — and a flat bomb would be worthless by biome 3.
Swarm Logic: damage multiplier while the arena is crowded.

Hard bound on any bulk purchase, xMax included.  The loop below terminates on its own for every upgrade the game actually ships — it stops the moment a level is unaffordable or capped. This is the guard for the case that is not true: a line that is both free and uncapped would spin forever, and the first anyone would know is the game hanging on a button press. Tolerance for "can the player afford this".  Upgrade costs are fractional (6.0, then 6.9, then 7.94...) and Catnip is accumulated by repeated addition, so exact affordability is a float-EQUALITY question, and float equality does not hold: a player holding precisely the price of two levels has `12.9 - 6.0 == 6.899999999999999`, which is not `>= 6.9`, so the second level is refused.  That is not a theoretical concern — it is what xMax does on every press. It also made the bulk preview and the bulk purchase disagree, because the two walk the same numbers in a different order and land on different last bits. Caught by check_hud, 2026-08-20.

Kills only ever pay Catnip now — Catnip is Reawaken-only (GameState header). CAT BURGLAR'S CUT: damage that would have been thrown away is sold instead.  The ratio is CAPPED. Overkill divided by max health is unbounded - a late build one-shotting a common mouse wastes hundreds of times its health - and an uncapped version would pay hundreds of rewards for a single kill.

ECHO: a second, weaker aura that lags a beat behind the cat.  ONE zone, dropped on a cadence and living exactly as long as the cadence, so there is never more than one of it. The aura trail card drops many short-lived zones and smears; this drops one and lags, which is the difference between a trail and an echo - and the reason it is not simply the trail with a different number.

EDGE_BURN: mice near the rim of the play area take damage over time, so the ones wandering off are not simply lost.  Expressed as a fraction of aura DPS for the usual reason — a flat number would vanish by biome 3. The band is generous because its job is to catch strays, not to be a second aura the player has to stand in.

How hard a FLEEING enemy is pulled back toward the middle of the play area, as a weight against its run-away direction (0 = straight away, 1 = as much centre-seeking as fleeing).  Reported 2026-08-18: "golden mice are sometimes too hard to catch, they disappear too fast". They were not timing out — they were running in a straight line and crossing the bounds, which despawns them. Fleeing directly away from the player means the shortest path to safety is always the nearest edge, so the better the player chased, the faster the treat left.  With a centre bias the golden still flees, but it ARCS: cornered against an edge it curves back inward along it instead of stepping out. That makes the chase longer and the catch possible without touching its speed or lifetime, both of which would have changed how much it is worth.

How much faster a FLIER crosses the play area than a ground enemy.  Lives here rather than in EnemyData for the same reason `speed_px_per_sec` does: movement is a presentation and pacing choice, not a balance value. What a flier is WORTH is authored in /data; how fast it looks is authored here.  Fast enough that it is a moment rather than a fixture — a flier the player can amble over to is just a mouse that ignores puddles.
radians/sec of random heading drift

Stage 1 is the baseline; each of the five bosses grants one, and the ending grants the seventh.  Spelled out rather than derived as `BOSS_REALMS.size() + 1` — GDScript will not accept a method call in a constant expression, and a `var` here would put a mutable global in front of the one number the damage curve is built on. check_damage.gd asserts the two stay in step. Five bosses need SIX stages: get_evolution_stage() counts consecutive clears down BOSS_REALMS and returns clears + 1. Widening the ladder forces a re-spread of both evolution terms - the mirror of the rule that shortened the base to 5.04 when the ladder went from eight stages to four. It is 2.2449 now, and 2.2449^6 is still the same x128 the gate has always asserted. Seven, not six: stage 7 is the ENDING's - `final_boss_defeated` adds the last step (pawpocalypse.md ▸ Progression Rules). It was granted by Nine Lives until that layer was cut on 2026-09-14.

Fence: the Catnip multiplier earned by kills already made this wave.  The kill count is capped rather than the multiplier, so the wording on the node ("per kill, up to 100") stays true at every level instead of being true at some levels and silently clipped at others.

GRAND FINALE: the kittens the Magician switched off drag instead of bite.  Reaches only mice near a LIVE kitten, which is what makes this the kittens doing the work rather than a second Misdirection - the Magician gave up their damage and gets their presence back.

GRIDLOCK: the snared drag down whatever strays over them.  Fliers are the ONLY population this can reach, because everything on the ground is already inside an arena-wide Snare - so the capstone is written as "fliers near snared ground mice", which is what "the enemies touching them" amounts to once the ground is universally covered.  O(fliers x ground), not O(n squared): the outer loop skips everything that is not a flier first, and there are rarely many.
Infestation: spawn rate added per kill, and how fast that decays.

KITTEN_KILL_EXPLODES: a mouse that dies in a kitten's paws detonates.  A fraction of the VICTIM's max HP rather than of the player's damage, which is what the card says and also what makes it scale — enemy HP is the curve everything else in this game had to be pinned to.
kept below base_kitten_contact_radius so orbiting still counts as contact

How far a kitten's target may be over-subscribed before it rebalances onto a less crowded mouse. Must be >1: at exactly 1, two kittens on a 2-claim vs 1-claim pair would swap places every frame forever, which is the target flicker this system was built to avoid. At 2 the assignment converges and then stops moving.
How long a kitten holds one wander heading before picking another. Short enough to look alive, long enough not to jitter on the spot.

Roaming, for when there is nothing in detection range. A kitten frozen mid-screen reads as broken — the whole premise is that they are autonomous hunters, and a hunter that stands still looks like a bug in the behaviour than an absence of prey. They wander instead, which also spreads the pool out so the next spawn is more likely to land near someone.  Roaming is deliberately slower than the hunt: a kitten sprinting aimlessly looks panicked, and the speed difference makes "spotted something" legible without any other cue.
radians

Last Stand: damage multiplier while the arena is nearly empty.  THE MIRROR OF SWARM LOGIC, and owning both is deliberately not a permanent buff - there is a band in the middle where neither fires, so a player who buys both still has a reason to care how full the screen is.
Levy: kills between payouts, and the multiple of a reward each one pays.
Long Lunch: Catnip owed for the stillness banked so far, as a multiple of a single reward. Capped, for the same reason Carry is: an uncapped bank pays for walking away.

Bounded so a long run with a fast trail cannot grow this without limit — the trail drops on a fixed cadence, so the ceiling is only ever hit if the cadence and lifetime are retuned badly, and silently leaking zones would be worse.

Added to a biome's authored Golden Mouse chance, not multiplied — a biome with no goldens at all should stay that way, and a multiplier on 0.0 is 0.0 either way, but an addition says the intent out loud.  Clamped: a golden chance at or above 1.0 would mean the pool never rolls, and every enemy in the game would be a Golden Mouse.

Hard ceiling on live mice, regardless of spawn rate. Tier 8 at a maxed Spawn Rate is ~40 spawns/second against a ~16 second wander, which is several hundred live Node2Ds all running _process and _draw. "The screen feels empty" is a design problem; "the screen is a slideshow" is a worse one, and this is the cheapest place to bound it.
Bounded because signature kills are frequent and the pool is pre-sized: the realm reserves exactly this much headroom above the purchasable maximum.

A ceiling on the wave index. Nothing should reach it - the deepest measured run tops out around 35 - but HP rises 1.35 a wave and an unbounded index would overflow a float long before it stopped being fun.
The narrowest arena the game still works in. Below this the edge-burn band has no room on the X axis, the spawner's edge positions collapse together and the boss arena is thinner than the boss.
One frame at 60fps. A Timer cannot fire faster than the frame rate, so this is the point past which the spawn rate has to be delivered as a batch per tick rather than as a shorter interval.

THE MOUNT FOLLOWS THE UNICORN NODE (designer, 2026-09-14: "when the unicorn is awakened it should stay awakened. So the player should have the unicorn ... mount follows the node"). The stage the cat LOOKS is the earned stage or the first mounted stage, whichever is higher, so buying the Unicorn puts the cat on it that moment regardless of the boss ladder - and a boss kill past that point still advances the mount through Alicorn and Void Unicorn. The damage ladder (get_evolution_stage) is untouched: the node is a purchase, the multipliers are earned.
What counts as "already nearly dead" for Play With Food.

How far the cat may drift and still count as standing still, per frame. Not zero: the cursor jitters by a pixel on most hardware, and a hard equality would mean Carry never charged for anyone holding a real mouse.
Shards needed before the screen goes off.
Compound Interest: share of banked Catnip paid per minute of real time.
